dedupe_keys.name: portuguese critical infrastructure wildfire exposure pipeline

description: This Python pipeline prepares a per-asset wildfire exposure screen for critical infrastructure in a Portuguese pilot area around Sever do Vouga. It extracts schools, substations, water plants and emergency facilities from OpenStreetMap, joins satellite and terrain products, builds fuel and burn-scar layers, and emits scored GeoParquet assets through a STAC catalog. The repository publishes scripts, schema and provenance documentation, a static geobrowser and pilot outputs for 3,045 assets. A modeller could use the asset table to prioritise exposure scenarios or reuse the preparation steps with a new area of interest and its source layers. Scores are ranks within the assessed area, not probabilities, fire-spread outputs or live operational warnings. The authors compared the pilot score against 2025 burns after the 2024 input window, but only five assets were labelled burned; their report says that this cannot isolate which features carry the signal. This review checked documentation and file metadata, not the large raster or Parquet payloads or runtime. The MIT licence covers project code; OSM, Copernicus and national layers retain separate terms. Related source resources are the OSM asset inventory and Portuguese burn history; this repository is the distinct scored-asset preparation pipeline.
